title: validate_deterministic_item: accepts indefinite-length CBOR
description:
Root Cause: The validate_deterministic_item function in credential.rs (line 244-246) has an overly permissive else branch that returns Ok(()) for any CBOR type not explicitly handled. The input [0x9f, 0x01, 0xff] is an indefinite-length array (0x9f = indefinite array marker), which should be rejected per RFC 8949 Section 4.2.3 (deterministic CBOR forbids indefinite-length encoding). Since 0x9f falls outside the handled ranges (maps 0xa1-0xb7, arrays 0x80-0x97), it falls through to the else branch and incorrectly returns Ok(()).

Affected Test: malformed_or_unbound_credentials_are_rejected

Location: /Volumes/Attic/Desktop/Projects/crates/oscore/src/edhoc/credential.rs:244-246

Suggested Fix: Change the else branch at lines 244-246 to reject indefinite-length markers. Replace: } else { Ok(()) } with: } else { if (first & 0x1f) == 0x1f && first >= 0x40 { return Err(EdhocError::InvalidMessage); } Ok(()) } -- This checks for major types 2-5 with additional info 31 (the indefinite-length markers 0x5f, 0x7f, 0x9f, 0xbf) and the break code 0xff.

Error Type: Logic error - overly permissive validation
